title: Investigative talking points
rankingMethod: Editorial triage by evidence strength, allocation scale and verifiable next question; not corruption likelihood or a statistical risk score. Amounts overlap; do not add them.

findings.title: RCS: identical budget packages across unequal rainfall proxies
findings.basis: Direct allocation observation; rainfall need remains a proxy
findings.question: What policy or engineering design justifies one identical budget unit per office?
findings.evidence: All district-office RCS lines have the same amount. Province/regional rainfall proxies differ by 2.59×. Alternative formulas move different numbers of budget units. All 199 DEO lines are retained unchanged in HGAB; no differentiated needs weighting is visible in the amounts.
findings.alternative: Standard package costs or a minimum coverage policy may justify equal allocations. Rainfall alone does not measure demand.
findings.next: Obtain siting, design capacity, water demand, catchment area and existing RCS inventory.
findings.caution: DEO is not LEG; province rainfall is not a district observation. Returning FY2026 program.

findings.title: HGAB-only domestic candidates: verify the counterpart before calling an insertion
findings.question: Which candidates are genuinely absent from NEP after wording, scope and occurrence review?
findings.evidence: Native schedule totals reconcile; unmatched domestic records remain distinct from unpaired FAP review lines.
findings.alternative: Wrapped titles, OCR, changes in office or PAP, renaming and aggregated occurrences can hide counterparts.
findings.next: Stratified original-page adjudication; estimate false positives before extrapolating counts.
findings.caution: Do not adopt another analyst’s additions count as ground truth. FAPs take a separate review path.

findings.title: Multi-purpose buildings: a large share needs NEP counterpart review
findings.question: Which MPB lines are genuinely new, and what documented facility needs and designs support them?
findings.evidence: The HGAB MPB PAP contains 5,765 lines carrying ₱83.707B. 620 counterpart cases remain separate from insertion candidates. The historical screen has 329 comparison pairs covering 301 distinct NEP proposals.
findings.alternative: Renaming, combined occurrences and legitimate phased construction can explain unmatched or recurring titles. Similar amounts can reflect standard designs.
findings.next: Audit original NEP/HGAB pages; obtain building purpose, floor area, design, quantities, contract scope and completion records.
findings.caution: MPB overlaps the full DPWH insertion/repeat findings; do not add their amounts. Equal allocations are not equal construction unit prices.

findings.title: Recurring project titles: inspect overlapping work before alleging duplication
findings.lead: 634 of 736 NEP comparison pairs clearly retained in HGAB
findings.question: Are new appropriations paying for already-funded components or legitimate continuation?
findings.evidence: 591 of 685 distinct NEP repeat-screen proposals have clear HGAB links. 22 proposals have explicit overlapping historical chainage. ₱27.255B is the unique NEP proposal allocation, not alleged loss.
findings.alternative: Multi-year implementation, rehabilitation and distinct components can share names and segments.
findings.next: Prioritize explicitly overlapping retained proposals and high amounts; compare contracts, quantities, tranche scopes and completion.
findings.caution: The 737 headline counts NEP–old GAA comparison pairs. Potential retention and missing counterparts remain separate.

findings.title: Exact ₱5M road and flood allocations cluster in the same offices
findings.lead: 35 overlapping offices vs 21.7 expected under independence
findings.question: Does standard design, office workload or coordinated allocation explain the co-occurrence?
findings.evidence: Office odds ratio 5.34; unadjusted exact p=5.07e-06. Region-controlled result is also unusual under its stated null.
findings.alternative: Common specifications, office workload and project mix can create clustering.
findings.next: Pre-specify work-type and workload controls; inspect quantities and comparable prior-year prices.
findings.caution: Threshold/category selection was post hoc. Association does not establish procurement splitting or intent.

findings.title: INSPIRE: a large returning named appropriation needs a whole-project ledger
findings.question: What is the total approved cost and which unfinished components explain the new appropriation?
findings.evidence: Named GAA lines exist in FY2023 and FY2025; FY2027 is not a first appearance.
findings.alternative: A legitimate phased project can require multiple appropriations.
findings.next: Obtain total project cost, phases, progress, obligations, disbursements and procurement records.
findings.caution: Appropriations are not actual spending; stage/year sums do not prove duplication.

findings.title: Length and chainage gaps limit budget scrutiny
findings.lead: Roads: 48.69% · Bridges: 94.74% · FMR: 99.69% without usable extracted length
findings.basis: Extracted metadata coverage; original-document completeness unverified
findings.question: Can the funded segment and engineering length be established for every allocation?
findings.evidence: Roads: 3,334/6,498 lines have derivable stated lengths · Bridges: 60/1,140 lines have derivable stated lengths · FMR: 3/964 lines have derivable stated lengths. Official programs have separate denominators on the supporting page.
findings.alternative: Lengths may be recorded in engineering schedules or continuation text not recovered by this extraction; incomplete metadata need not reflect deliberate omission.
findings.next: Inspect original source pages and obtain funded-segment boundaries, complete chainage, project quantities and bridge spans; reconcile extraction gaps before alleging disclosure failures.
findings.caution: Missing includes absent and unusable extracted evidence, not proof the original documents lack length. Coordinate distances do not establish construction length; mixed scopes are separate.

findings.title: Allocation per stated meter: inspect scope before comparing rates
findings.lead: 220 road and 2 bridge high-rate candidates · FMR peers insufficient
findings.basis: Descriptive allocation/segment-length proxy; comparable engineering costs unavailable
findings.question: Do apparently high rates reflect short printed segments, structures, broader funded scope, or unusually costly comparable work?
findings.evidence: Whole HGAB line-item allocation is divided by its derivable stated segment meters. Roads, bridges and FMR are displayed separately, with official work-program filters. Mixed road/bridge lines receive no single-work rate. Data-derived length groups and within-program slope-change screens are provided; no fixed 100-meter boundary is imposed.
findings.alternative: Terrain, width, structures, approaches, rehabilitation scope and components outside the stated segment can explain large differences. Tiny printed ranges or parser errors can produce extreme ratios.
findings.next: Verify station endpoints on original pages, then compare quantities, width, funded extent, designs and bill-of-quantity costs within the same work type. Investigate unusually short denominators before interpreting extreme ratios.
findings.caution: These are appropriations per stated segment meter, not verified construction unit costs. Bridge chainage is not necessarily bridge span. No cross-category average, overpricing estimate or corruption probability is established.

findings.title: Very short printed road ranges need engineering clarification
findings.lead: 3 checked road ranges imply less than 5 meters
findings.basis: Original PDF text agreement; funded engineering extent unresolved
findings.question: Do the printed station endpoints correctly describe the funded segment, or do notation and scope need correction?
findings.evidence: Original-page visible text agrees with sampled road titles whose station differences calculate to 0.587 meters, 1.49 meters, 4.67 meters. Across all 3,175 known road lengths, only 204 (6.43%) are below 100 meters; high-rate sorting concentrates short denominators at the top.
findings.alternative: A source-document typo, station convention, short component within a larger project, or broader funded scope can explain these values. A very short printed range does not establish the physical length actually funded.
findings.next: Request corrected or certified station endpoints, funded-segment plans, engineering quantities and allocation scope; verify notation before interpreting extreme allocation-per-meter rates.
findings.caution: This is a printed-range/denominator issue, not evidence that most road projects are short or overpriced. Sampled title agreement rules out a title-transcription mismatch for those examples, not source errors or engineering ambiguity. Bridge lengths require separate interpretation.

rcs.correlation: Undefined: allocation variance is zero; no correlation p-value reported.

highRateScreen.method: Peers share category, official PAP and a data-derived length band; at least 20 peers with stated length ≥10m. Candidate rate exceeds both 2× peer median and Q3+1.5×IQR. Chart extremes exceed max(2×median,Q3+3×IQR); sub-10m printed ranges also stay off rate charts.
highRateScreen.limits: Exploratory relative-rate screen, not proof of overpricing. Width, terrain, structures, engineering quantities and funded extent remain unverified. Missing or insufficient peers produce no high-rate conclusion.

scope: FY2027 NEP/HGAB 3rd reading; historical GAA comparisons where locally available. No GAB/GAA 2027 outcome inferred.

lineItemReviewQueue.ranking: Flag count descending, allocation pesos descending, occurrence ID ascending for exact ties.
lineItemReviewQueue.scope: Domestic DPWH HGAB 3rd-reading occurrences only; not a ranking of the entire national budget.

method.amountGroupScope: Identical PAP and positive exact peso amount; counts are allocation occurrences, not certified distinct construction contracts.
method.historicalMatch: Identical full normalized title after complete trailing metadata removal; same qualified municipality/province; direction/location/tranche conflict and disjoint stated chainage excluded.
method.weights: One point per flag type. Multiple historical years do not add points.
method.highMeterRate: Peers share category, official PAP and a data-derived length band; at least 20 peers with stated length ≥10m. Candidate rate exceeds both 2× peer median and Q3+1.5×IQR. Chart extremes exceed max(2×median,Q3+3×IQR); sub-10m printed ranges also stay off rate charts.
method.evidenceGaps: Missing length, sub-10m printed ranges and insufficient peers are cautions, not points. Extreme rates require denominator/scope review and are omitted from rate charts.
method.summaryCoverage: Nine summary findings are not nine independent line-item flags. RCS equal amounts use the amount-group flag; MPB is a program scope; INSPIRE is outside this DPWH queue. Length gaps and very short printed ranges are evidence cautions. Historical recurrence and overlap support the repeat finding.
method.dependence: Historical recurrence and chainage overlap are related indicators; scores are descriptive triage, not independent evidence or probabilities.
limitations: Uniform packages can be legitimate. Exact appropriation amounts are not unit costs.
Strict historical matching misses paraphrased titles and unresolved locations; no flag means insufficient evidence, not clearance.
The prior-year search uses locally available DPWH road, bridge, building and flood records, not every agency/year.
Matching/parser errors can produce insertion flags. Top 25 overlap other findings; do not sum them as losses.
Current office, representative, role and party do not contribute any points.

districtComparisonPolicy.scope: All district rows are available for reader selection in the all-district ranking. No selected-district section or person-specific defaults.

localDatasetInventory.use: Potential socio-economic context; no year/definition recorded in the inspected rows, so not used as a needs control.
Historical project reference; not a current flood-exposure or FY2027 needs denominator.
